# rig (device class)

> Transceivers with CAT or PTT control — one shared rigctld for every program

Amateur transceivers as a family: a radio reached over CAT (computer-aided transceiver control) through a serial port, or a radio with no CAT at all that is keyed by a serial control line through an interface. One class because what Linux needs — serial access through `dialout` and a stable port path — is the same for all of them, and the radio-specific detail (hamlib model, port, speed, how it is keyed) lives in each radio's own manifest.

## Devices in this class

- [btech-uv-50pro](btech-uv-50pro.md)
- [yaesu-ft-991a](yaesu-ft-991a.md)

## Shared setup

Join `dialout` and log out and back in — group membership does not reach a session already open. Say which radio is on the station with `hammunition station set --rig <device> --rig-device <by-id path> --rig-baud <rate>`, then install the `rig-service` unit (it ships in the `station` profile). There is no udev rule to write: /dev/serial/by-id/ already names the port.
